headline: 3-of-5 OneSig multisig owns immutable EndpointV2 + ULN libs; T2 fee/default-config powers with zero delay, no on-chain gov or SC
short_headline: T2 multisig control on immutable core (no timelock)

findings.text: EndpointV2 (0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c, eid 30101) owner() returns 0xBe010A7e3686FdF65E93344ab664D065A0B02478 (custom OneSig 3/5 multisig) via https://defipunkd.com/api/contract/read?chainId=1&address=0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c&method=owner at block 25381238 and surfacer page.

No proxy pattern, no implementation()/admin() storage; immutable per incident report and contract read (no upgrade surface). Message libraries (SendUln302 0xbB2Ea70C9E858123480642Cf96acbcCE1372dCe1, ReceiveUln302) are append-only immutable once deployed; new libs registerable but existing ones unmodifiable.

No timelock, no multi-stage execution path (voting/scheduler/execute), no MIN_DELAY or queue. Direct multisig execution on owner-controlled functions (registerLibrary, setDefaultUlnConfigs, setTreasury, withdrawFee).

Primary control multisig is custom OneSig (5 signers, 3 threshold, executorRequired=true, 1 executor) at 0xBe010A7e3686FdF65E93344ab664D065A0B02478. DVN contracts use separate per-operator signer quorums (e.g. LZ DVN at 0x589dEDbD617e0CBcB916A9223F4d1300c294236b). No other reachable multisigs on T1/T2 paths enumerated.
No on-chain Governor, OZ Governor, Aragon, or token-weighted voting. No proposalThreshold/votingPeriod/quorum/timelock constants readable.
No pause(), whenNotPaused, PAUSE_ROLE, guardian, or emergency role on EndpointV2. Explicitly cannot be paused or modified per incident report.

Highest reachable tier T2 on uncontested fast path: setDefaultUlnConfigs / setDefaultExecutorConfigs (affects default security posture for unset OApps), setTreasury / withdrawFee / withdrawLzTokenFee (fee redirection), registerLibrary (adds new verification paths). No T1 (immutable Endpoint/libs hold no user funds; no mint/pause-withdraw/upgrade-to-drain functions). 3/5 OneSig fails Security Council criteria (>=7 signers + >=50% non-insider public).

steelman.red: A 3/5 insider-controlled custom OneSig can immediately execute T2 actions (fee redirection, default security config changes) with zero delay and no on-chain check, and past multisig incidents show operational risk.
steelman.orange: T2 powers (fee redirection, default ULN/executor configs, library registration) sit with a 3/5 custom OneSig multisig (fails SC criteria) on zero-delay path with no timelock or on-chain governance, while immutable design caps at T2 and OApp owners independently control per-channel security stacks.
steelman.green: Core EndpointV2 and deployed message libraries are fully immutable with no upgrade/pause surface reachable by any actor (including the multisig), and OApp owners retain exclusive control over their security configuration and delegate powers with no protocol-level T1 blast radius.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because T2 economic/operational powers are held by a 3/5 custom OneSig multisig (failing Security Council signer/threshold/non-insider rules) with zero timelock and no on-chain governance on the fast path, exactly matching orange criteria; immutable cores prevent T1 while green would require max tier T3/T4 or SC-protected T1/T2.

evidence.shows: EndpointV2 contract info, ABI (owner/transferOwnership/renounceOwnership/registerLibrary/setConfig/setDefaultSendLibrary etc.), read results at block 25381235 including getRegisteredLibraries and isSendingMessage=false; no proxy/implementation/paused detected.
owner() returns 0xBe010A7e3686FdF65E93344ab664D065A0B02478 at block 25381238 (rawReturnData confirms).
SendUln302: owner()/transferOwnership/renounceOwnership present; setDefaultUlnConfigs, setDefaultExecutorConfigs, setTreasury, withdrawFee etc.; no proxy, no paused, immutable direct contract.

EndpointV2 at 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c is immutable and cannot be upgraded/paused/modified by anyone including LayerZero Labs; message libraries append-only immutable; OApp delegate/owner controls per-channel security stack; LZ DVN admin/relay limited, signers control admin via quorumChangeAdmin; no super-admin escape hatch.
OneSig custom multisig (not Gnosis Safe): 5 signers, threshold 3, executorRequired=true, 1 executor; functions setSigner/setThreshold/setExecutor etc.; surfaced signer addresses.
OneSig contract (verified): custom signature-based multisig with 5 signers/3 threshold/executor model; executeTransaction, setSigner/setThreshold etc.; no standard Safe interface.
LayerZero Labs uses multisig for Endpoint ownership; users relying on defaults are fully reliant on the LayerZero Labs multisig; plans to raise threshold to 7-of-10 and deploy OneSig.

unknowns: C4: exact signer identities, employment status (insider vs non-insider), and public announcement status for the 5 OneSig signers not re-verified beyond contract structure and LZ context; DVN-specific signer sets per operator not exhaustively enumerated for all chains.

protocol_metadata.about: LayerZero V2 is an immutable omnichain messaging protocol connecting 60+ blockchains. OApps send arbitrary messages, tokens (OFT), or calls via EndpointV2; security is configured per-OApp via pluggable DVN stacks chosen by the OApp owner/delegate. Message verification uses off-chain DVN attestations submitted on-chain; execution uses permissionless executors. Core contracts (EndpointV2, ULN302 libs) are immutable with append-only library registration.

headline: Permissionless on-chain messaging with no pause/ gating on EndpointV2 or libs; no user-fund custody or admin-blockable claims; immutable core

findings.text: Core contracts (EndpointV2, SendUln302, ReceiveUln302) expose no user-fund custody/exit functions (withdraw/redeem/burn/claim); messaging is send() / lzReceive() / composeQueue() permissionless (pay fees). App-specific exits (OFT burn/redeem) live in downstream OApp contracts, not core.
No access modifiers (onlyRole/onlyOwner/whenNotPaused) gate core receive/claim paths on EndpointV2; immutable and owner functions limited to config/library registration (not message delivery).
No pause guards, paused(), isPaused(), PAUSE_ROLE, or GUARDIAN on EndpointV2 or registered libs. Explicitly cannot be paused per incident report. No max pause duration or uncapped pause callable.
No emergency-pause path separate from governance; no pause mechanism exists at all on core Endpoint.
No queued redemption, daily caps, or pausable queue on core messaging layer.
No forced-exit/escape-hatch needed; messaging is permissionless and censorship-resistant by design (immutable Endpoint delivers verified messages without admin gate).
All core functions (send, lzReceive, setPeer, setConfig per OApp) directly callable on-chain via Etherscan write tab, generic wallets, or SDKs with no frontend dependency.

steelman.red: If any admin could pause message claims or require signatures for finalized delivery, users could be trapped; historical DVN incidents show downstream risks but core itself has no such gate.
steelman.orange: While core has no pause, downstream OApps using single-DVN configs can experience delivery issues or forgery under adversarial conditions, and some bridges built on it may introduce their own exit queues/pauses.
steelman.green: EndpointV2 and message libs are immutable with zero pause surface or admin gating on message delivery/claims; send/receive paths are fully permissionless and directly on-chain callable; no user principal is custodied by the core protocol.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because the immutable EndpointV2 has no pause, no admin-gated exit/claim functions, and permissionless messaging paths that any wallet can call directly; downstream app-specific custody/exit risks belong to those OApps, not the core messaging layer.

evidence.shows: EndpointV2 ABI and reads: send/lzReceive/composeQueue/ setPeer etc. present and callable; no paused/pause-related functions or state; owner functions do not gate message delivery.
Endpoint cannot be upgraded, paused, or modified by anyone; delivers verified messages; OApp owner controls security config but core delivery is immutable and ungated.
SendUln302: no pause mechanism; config functions are owner-only but do not gate message verification/delivery for already-configured paths.

protocol_metadata.about: LayerZero V2 is an immutable omnichain messaging protocol. Core contracts do not custody user funds; they provide permissionless send/receive of arbitrary messages and token transfers (via OFT standards in OApps). Security and execution are configured per application.

headline: Relies on off-chain DVN signer committees for message verification (OApp-configurable); LZ multisig can register new libs; impacted TVS under single-DVN failure: material for apps using defaults (~high % of early paths)

findings.text: Core EndpointV2 does not make external on-chain calls to oracles/price feeds/lending pools in normal operation; verification is off-chain DVN ECDSA signatures submitted via relay() on DVN contracts. DVN liveness/honesty is critical for delivery and forgery resistance.

DVNs use off-chain multisig signer committees (e.g. LZ DVN signers held by LayerZero Labs; quorum required to change signer set or admin). Admin role limited to relay (cannot forge or change signers unilaterally). Post-KelpDAO, LZ DVN enforces baseline multi-DVN requirement on channels it participates in.
No material canonical bridge dependency for core messaging layer (LayerZero is the messaging substrate used by many bridges/OFTs). Cross-chain is native to the protocol design.
No nested collateral/restaking chain in core; OFT/wrapped assets are app-level.
No forkedFrom lineage recorded in DeFiLlama context for this assessment.

Fallbacks: OApp owners can configure multiple required/optional DVNs + thresholds + block confirmations (getConfig/setConfig on Endpoint). LZ DVN now refuses sole-required-DVN channels. No on-chain sanity-check circuit breakers on core Endpoint for bad attestations beyond DVN quorum. Fallbacks are LIVE and user-configurable (not protocol-enforced defaults).
No sequencer/DA dependency beyond base-chain substrate; operates on many L1/L2s permissionlessly.

Executors (permissionless off-chain bots) are required for lzReceive gas abstraction on destination; failure degrades UX (user can still call lzReceive directly) but does not cause principal loss or insolvency.

Endpoint owner (OneSig multisig) can registerLibrary (new verification libs) and setDefault*Configs without timelock or exit window for existing OApps using defaults. New libs are immutable once added but could introduce new off-chain DVN deps if adopted.

steelman.red: Off-chain DVN signer compromise (as in KelpDAO 1/1 case) can forge messages leading to principal loss in downstream apps; LZ multisig can introduce new libs/defaults affecting many channels without user exit window.
steelman.orange: Message verification depends on off-chain DVN committees (liveness + honesty); single-DVN configs (historically common on defaults) create forgery risk materializing in ecosystem, and multisig can register new verification surfaces without timelock, but OApp owners can override with multi-DVN stacks and LZ DVN now enforces stronger baselines.
steelman.green: Core contracts are immutable with no external on-chain deps that can steal principal; all security configuration is OApp-owner controlled and permissionlessly overridable; executor liveness failure is graceful (direct lzReceive still works); no protocol-level principal custody.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because verification security critically depends on off-chain DVN signer committees (with historical single-DVN forgery incident causing downstream principal loss) and the LZ multisig can register new libs/default configs without exit window, while OApp-level overrides and post-incident LZ DVN policy provide meaningful but incomplete mitigation; impacted TVS under DVN failure is material for default-using apps.

evidence.shows: DVN security model: off-chain signers produce attestations; admin relays only; signers control admin via quorumChangeAdmin; LZ DVN now refuses sole-required attestor; 1/1 DVN stack allowed forgery leading to $292M loss in KelpDAO rsETH; Endpoint immutable.
EndpointV2 getRegisteredLibraries includes ULN302 libs; setConfig per OApp for ULN/DVN selection; no external oracle/price-feed calls in core ABI.
OApp configures required/optional DVNs, thresholds, confirmations per pathway; defaults provided by LayerZero but overridable.

unknowns: A2: exact current signer sets, quorums, and diversification for all active DVNs (beyond LZ DVN) not re-enumerated on-chain for every chain/EID.
A9: whether newly registered libs have been adopted in default configs or high-TVS OApps since last snapshot.

protocol_metadata.about: LayerZero V2 provides immutable omnichain messaging. Security depends on OApp-chosen DVN stacks (off-chain signers) and permissionless executors. No core contract holds or can unilaterally move user principal.

headline: Fully permissionless contracts: anyone can deploy OApp, setPeer, send/receive messages (pay fees); no whitelist/KYC/operator gate; independent SDK/third-party paths exist

findings.text: No onlyWhitelisted/onlyRole/allowlist/isKYCed modifiers on user entry points (send, lzReceive, setPeer, setConfig per OApp, registerLibrary is owner-only but not user admission). Anyone can deploy OApp and configure.
No off-chain operator approval required to admit send/receive/claim actions. DVN/executor liveness affects delivery but not admission (permissionless placement).

Official frontend/website ToS contains standard sanctions/jurisdictional boilerplate (A3-passive); no runtime IP geo-blocking or wallet screening enforcement detected on core contracts. Context only, does not affect grade.

Independent access paths exist: official Solidity SDK + examples in docs.layerzero.network and GitHub LayerZero-Labs/LayerZero-v2; third-party frontends/bridges (Stargate, many OFT deployments, aggregators) route through contracts; wallet integrations (MetaMask, Safe apps) and direct Etherscan write calls all work without official publisher cooperation.
No on-chain sanctions blocklist or OFAC oracle check in EndpointV2 or ULN libs; admission is unconditional.
Read access fully permissionless (anyone can call view functions/getConfig/getRegisteredLibraries). Write access (send, setPeer per OApp, lzReceive) also permissionless (gas + fees).
ToS on layerzero.network contains standard eligibility/sanctions language; verbatim extraction not performed in this run but does not gate contract admission.

steelman.red: If contracts required whitelist signatures or on-chain KYC oracle checks, or a single operator had to approve every message, admission would be captured.
steelman.orange: Contracts are theoretically open but if no SDK/third-party frontend/aggregator existed, practical access would be limited to official UI only.
steelman.green: Contracts have no whitelist/KYC/operator gate on any user action; send/receive/setConfig are fully permissionless and directly callable; multiple independent paths (SDK, third-party UIs, wallets, aggregators) exist and function without publisher cooperation.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because EndpointV2 and message libs impose zero contract-level whitelist, KYC, or operator approval on send/receive/config actions, and concrete independent access paths (official SDK + GitHub examples, third-party bridges/wallets/aggregators, direct on-chain calls) are live and usable.

evidence.shows: EndpointV2 ABI: send, lzReceive, setPeer, setConfig, setDelegate exposed without whitelist modifiers; only owner-gated functions are registerLibrary/setDefault* (not user admission).
Anyone can implement OApp, call setPeer on Endpoint, configure DVN/executor stacks permissionlessly; examples and SDK provided.
Public repo with full source, examples, and SDK guidance for direct contract interaction without official frontend.

protocol_metadata.about: LayerZero V2 messaging is fully permissionless at the contract level. Any developer can deploy an OApp, peer it, and send/receive messages by paying fees; security config is owner-controlled per channel.

headline: Bytecode verified on Etherscan + public GitHub source match; audits exist (Paladinsec V2 + C4 endpoint contests) but no recent recognized-firm coverage of main EVM deployment; immutable so low drift risk
short_headline: Verified + public repo; audit coverage partial/stale

findings.text: EndpointV2 and ULN302 libs verified on Etherscan (ABI sourced from Etherscan in defipunkd /api/contract/abi and surfacer pages); no 'Similar Match' issue on standard patterns; proxy not present so implementation verification not applicable.

Source in public GitHub LayerZero-Labs/LayerZero-v2 corresponds to deployed contracts (structure, EndpointV2.sol, ULN302 libs match explorer-visible source per repo description and docs). No pinned commit SHA for exact bytecode diff in this run.

Audit reports exist: Paladinsec V2 audit (2023) covering EndpointV2 on multiple chains; Code4rena contests for Endpoint V2 on Sui/Stellar/Starknet (2025). No audit_links pinned in context; recent EVM mainnet differential audit not located.

Paladinsec not in recognized firm list (Trail of Bits, Zellic, Spearbit, OZ, ConsenSys Diligence, etc.). Code4rena is competitive contest, not traditional firm audit. No recognized-firm audit covering current main EVM deployment found in this run.
Immutable contracts + append-only libs mean low material drift risk since deployment/audits. No post-audit code changes possible on deployed bytecode.
No proxies detected on EndpointV2 or ULN libs; direct verified implementations.

steelman.red: If bytecode were unverified or source unavailable, outsiders could not confirm behavior.
steelman.orange: Bytecode is verified and source is public and corresponding, but audit coverage relies on older/unknown-firm or contest reports without recent recognized-firm re-audit of main EVM contracts; exact commit-to-bytecode match not re-verified this run.
steelman.green: All core contracts are verified on explorers, source is public and structurally matches, and immutable design plus existing audit history (even if not recent recognized-firm) allows independent confirmation of behavior with minimal drift risk.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because bytecode is Etherscan-verified with public GitHub source correspondence and immutable design caps drift, but audit coverage is from older unknown-firm report + contests without recent recognized-firm audit of the primary EVM deployment meeting the green threshold exactly.

evidence.shows: ABI sourced from Etherscan; contract verified status implicit; full ABI and read results available for independent inspection.
Public repository with EndpointV2.sol, message libraries (ULN302), OApp standards; docs and examples match deployed behavior described in protocol docs and incident report.
V2 audit (completed Dec 2023) covering EndpointV2 on Ethereum and other chains; findings on governance/config but contracts audited pre some deployments.
Recent Code4rena contest audit for Endpoint V2 on Sui (Sep 2025); similar architecture to EVM V2.

unknowns: V2: exact commit SHA matching currently deployed bytecode on Ethereum not pinned or diff-verified in this run (scope limit).

V3/V4: no recent recognized-firm (Spearbit/Trail of Bits/etc.) audit report specifically covering the main EVM EndpointV2/ULN302 deployment post-2023 found; contest reports and older Paladinsec used instead.

protocol_metadata.about: LayerZero V2 immutable messaging contracts are verified on block explorers with public source available. Security model relies on configurable DVNs; core logic has been subject to audits and contests though recent recognized-firm EVM coverage is limited.
